pr_title: Fix "missing method Fd" crash on Windows
pr_body:
This ensures that `IOStreams.Out` always keeps the original `Fd()` value even if it's wrapped as a Colorable stream for Windows in cases when enabling virtual terminal processing has failed.

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6147

Thanks everyone for all the debugging info. I also could not reproduce this on Windows 10 and PowerShell.exe/Command Prompt/Git Bash, but looking at the code I can see how this could have happened.

This line performs an unsafe cast: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/b53c2c37e972d7385911826504f1490747a5424c/internal/prompter/prompter.go#L29

In this context, "stdout" is forwarded from `IOStreams.Out`, which is initialized like so: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/b53c2c37e972d7385911826504f1490747a5424c/pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go#L435

Note that `colorable.NewColorable()` returns an `io.Writer`, which is not guaranteed to have a `Fd() uintptr` method, but when this value is later cast into a `terminal.FileWriter` for the purpose of Prompter, it is required to have that method and will crash if it doesn't. This is what our users have been experiencing in certain context.

Now, `colorable.NewColorable(f)` will almost always return the input argument `f` unchanged (this is why neither @vilmibm nor I could reproduce this), but in certain cases it will return a custom Writer. This case is defined as such:
- GOOS must be "windows";
- `f` must be connected to a terminal;
- Windows "virtual terminal processing" must _not_ already be enabled for `f`.

We always attempt to enable "virtual terminal processing" in gh, but depending on the user's environment and Windows version, patches, or settings, this is not guaranteed to succeed: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/b53c2c37e972d7385911826504f1490747a5424c/pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go#L427

When it doesn't, NewColorable will return a custom Writer and Prompter will choke on it.

I will attempt a fix soon. Thanks for your patience 🙇

review_comments: I like that you made this and `terminalSize` simpler.
Is this necessary because the Go compiler does not recognize that the `fileWriter` interface implements the `io.Writer` interface?

No, it's because without an explicit type, `bodyWriter` would become the exact same type as `IOStreams.Out`, which is `fileWriter`. Then, later in this function I want to reassign `bodyWriter` to another Writer which doesn't necessarily have the `Fd()` method, which isn't needed anyway.

Basically, I'm just narrowing down the interface for the purpose of the rest of the code in this function.
